questions.question: Find the two signs to interchange to correct the equation. 30 - 12 ÷ 3 × 2 + 4 = 122
questions.questionHtml:
Find the two signs to interchange to correct the equation.

30 - 12 ÷ 3 × 2 + 4 = 122
questions.solution:
2. - and ×

After interchanging the symbols, we get:

⇒ 30 × 12 ÷ 3 - 2 + 4 = 122

⇒ 360 ÷ 3 - 2 + 4 = 122

⇒ 120 - 2 + 4 = 122

⇒ 124 - 2 = 122

⇒ 122 = 122

questions.question: Find the missing term: 7, 22, 89, ____, 2677, 18740
questions.questionHtml: Find the missing term: 7, 22, 89, ____, 2677, 18740
questions.solution:
​7

7 × 3 + 1 = 21 + 1 = 22

22 × 4 + 1 = 88 + 1 = 89

89 × 5 + 1 = 445 + 1 = 446

446 × 6 + 1 = 2676 + 1 = 2677

2677 × 7 + 1 = 18379 + 1 = 18740

So, "446" is the missing term.

questions.question: Instruction: Identify the assumptions that must hold for the statement to be valid, then choose the correct option. Statement: The discovery of gravitational waves has provided strong evidence for Einstein's theory of general relativity, but it also opens up new possibilities for understanding the universe's most extreme phenomena, such as black holes and neutron stars. Assumptions : I. Gravitational waves offer new insights into the nature of the universe. II. Einstein's theory of general relativity has been conclusively proven by the discovery of gravitational waves. III. The study of gravitational waves will lead to new breakthroughs in astrophysics.
questions.questionHtml:
Instruction: Identify the assumptions that must hold for the statement to be valid, then choose the correct option.

Statement: The discovery of gravitational waves has provided strong evidence for Einstein's theory of general relativity, but it also opens up new possibilities for understanding the universe's most extreme phenomena, such as black holes and neutron stars.

Assumptions:

I. Gravitational waves offer new insights into the nature of the universe.

II. Einstein's theory of general relativity has been conclusively proven by the discovery of gravitational waves.

III. The study of gravitational waves will lead to new breakthroughs in astrophysics.

options.text: Only I and II are implicit
options.html: Only I and II are implicit

options.text: Only II and III are implicit
options.html: Only II and III are implicit

options.text: All I, II, and III are implicit
options.html: All I, II, and III are implicit

questions.solution:
I. Gravitational waves offer new insights into the nature of the universe. - Implicit (The statement implies that the discovery opens new possibilities for understanding extreme phenomena. That clearly assumes gravitational waves provide new insights.)

II. Einstein's theory of general relativity has been conclusively proven by the discovery of gravitational waves. - Implicit (The statement clearly implies that the discovery of gravitational waves has provided strong evidence for Einstein's theory of general relativity)

III. The study of gravitational waves will lead to new breakthroughs in astrophysics. - Not Implicit (The statement does not explicitly says it leads to breakthroughs will definitely occur, but rather mentions that it opens up new possibilities.)

So, only I and II are implicit.

questions.question: Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows. Statement: Fewer people applied for teaching posts this year. Conclusions: I. Teaching is losing popularity. II. Applicants may be seeking better-paying jobs.
questions.questionHtml:
Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows.

Statement: Fewer people applied for teaching posts this year.

Conclusions:

I. Teaching is losing popularity.

II. Applicants may be seeking better-paying jobs.
questions.solution:
I. Teaching is losing popularity. - False (A fall in applications does not definitively suggest a decline in popularity; it could be due to other factors.)

II. Applicants may be seeking better-paying jobs. - False (The statement doesn't mention salary or external factors, making this an assumption rather than a deduction.)

So, neither I nor II follows.

questions.question: In a 40 L solution, the ratio of acid to water is 5:3. How much water must be added to make it 1:1?
questions.questionHtml: In a 40 L solution, the ratio of acid to water is 5:3. How much water must be added to make it 1:1?
questions.solution:
Total parts = 5 + 3 = 8

Acid = 40 × 5 ÷ 8 = 25 L

Water = 40 × 3 ÷ 8 = 15 L

Water to be added = 25 − 15 = 10 L

questions.question: In a class of 80 students, 60% are girls. If 75% of the girls passed, how many girls failed?
questions.questionHtml: In a class of 80 students, 60% are girls. If 75% of the girls passed, how many girls failed?
questions.solution:
Total students = 80

Number of girls = 60 × 80 ÷ 100 = 48

Girls passed = 75 × 48 ÷ 100 = 36

Girls failed = 48 − 36 = 12
